title: Small, and the Words That Never Change

lessons.title: लहान (lahān) — small
lessons.gloss: small — the opposite of मोठा, and an adjective that refuses to agree with anything

segments.text: Last chapter gave you मोठा and the two rules it obeys. This word is its opposite and it breaks one of them.

segments.instruction: say moṭhaṁ ghar, then mājhaṁ ghar moṭhaṁ āhe
segments.source: [YOU RECALL: say *moṭhaṁ ghar*, then *mājhaṁ ghar moṭhaṁ āhe*]

segments.text: लहान — lahān — small, little; young.
लहान घर, लहान खोली, लहान मित्र — lahān ghar, lahān khoolī, lahān mitra.

Three genders, one form. लहान (lahān) does not end in -आ, so it has nothing to change, and it stays exactly as it is in front of any noun at all. Compare it with मोठा, which moved three ways one lesson ago, and the contrast tells you which kind of adjective you are holding.
It also does the work English splits between small and young: लहान (lahān) भाऊ is a younger brother, not a short one. Marathi treats age and size as the same scale for people.

Its history is a good one. Sanskrit लघु (laghu) meant "light, slight, small" — the same ancient word as Latin levis and English light. The Marathi form wore लघु down to लहान (lahān) over two thousand years, and the meaning barely moved.

segments.instruction: lahān ghar, lahān khoolī, lahān mitra — nothing moved
segments.source: [YOU SAY: *lahān ghar*, *lahān khoolī*, *lahān mitra* — nothing moved]

segments.instruction: moṭhaṁ ghar, moṭhī khoolī — and hear that something did
segments.source: [YOU SAY: *moṭhaṁ ghar*, *moṭhī khoolī* — and hear that something did]

segments.instruction: say म्हणणे and report that your room is small
segments.source: [YOU RECALL: say **म्हणणे** and report that your room is small]

segments.prompt: Put lahān on all three genders, then moṭhā on all three, and name the difference.
acceptedResponses: lahān ghar / khoolī / mitra; moṭhaṁ ghar, moṭhī khoolī, moṭhā mitra
लहान घर लहान खोली लहान मित्र मोठं घर मोठी खोली मोठा मित्र

feedback.correct: One never moves; the other moves three ways.

segments.text: How many forms does लहान (lahān) have? (One.) What does लहान (lahān) भाऊ mean? (A younger brother.)
Sources: Wiktionary: लहान (lahān).

lessons.title: The adjectives that never change
lessons.gloss: the adjectives that never agree — the class a learner who has met only मोठा will over-apply endings to

segments.text: Two adjectives, two behaviours. That is not an accident about those two words.

blocks.title: Grammar Lens: only the -आ adjectives agree

segments.text: Marathi's adjectives fall into two classes, and you can tell which class a word is in by looking at its last letter.

An adjective ending in -आ agrees: मोठा, मोठी, मोठं. An adjective ending in anything else does not agree at all, in any gender, ever: लहान (lahān) is लहान (lahān) in front of every noun in the language.
That second class is large, and most of it is words Marathi borrowed — from Sanskrit, from Persian, from Arabic. A borrowed word arrived without a Marathi ending to change, and it never grew one.

This is the mistake to watch for in yourself. Having met मोठा first, the temptation is to say लहानी खोली by analogy. It is wrong, and it is wrong in a way a listener notices immediately, because no Marathi speaker has ever heard that form. Check the last letter before you reach for an ending.

segments.instruction: moṭhī khoolī — and hear where the ending was earned
segments.source: [YOU SAY: *moṭhī khoolī* — and hear where the ending was earned]

segments.instruction: say शिकणे and that you are learning with a friend
segments.source: [YOU RECALL: say **शिकणे** and that you are learning with a friend]

segments.prompt: Say 'a small room' and then say what you must NOT say.

feedback.incorrect: lahān does not end in -ā, so nothing is added.

segments.text: What tells you whether an adjective will agree? (Its last letter — only -आ agrees.) Where do most of the non-agreeing ones come from? (Other languages — Sanskrit, Persian, Arabic.)

lessons.title: सुंदर (sundar) — beautiful
lessons.gloss: beautiful — a Sanskrit word Marathi took whole, endings and all, which is why it has none

segments.text: You have one word that never agrees. Here is a second, and knowing the class means you already know how it behaves before you meet it.
सुंदर — sundar — beautiful, lovely.
सुंदर घर, सुंदर खोली — sundar ghar, sundar khoolī — a beautiful house, a beautiful room.

No ending, in either gender, because सुंदर (sundar) does not end in -आ. You could predict that from the last letter one lesson before meeting the word, which is the whole return on having a class rather than a list.

The word came into Marathi from Sanskrit सुन्दर (sundara) unchanged, and that is exactly why it does not bend: it arrived already finished. Sanskrit built it from सु- (su-), "good, well" — the same prefix behind सुद्धा — so beautiful is, underneath, well-made.
It is a wide word in use. Marathi says सुंदर (sundar) of a person, a room, a song and a day, where English would reach for beautiful, lovely, nice and fine in turn.

segments.instruction: mājhyākaḍe sundar ghar āhe — I have a beautiful house
segments.source: [YOU SAY: *mājhyākaḍe sundar ghar āhe* — I have a beautiful house]

segments.instruction: say मिळणे and how it puts you in the dative
segments.source: [YOU RECALL: say **मिळणे** and how it puts you in the dative]

segments.prompt: Say 'a beautiful room' and 'a small beautiful house'.

feedback.incorrect: Both are invariable: no ending in any gender.

segments.text: Why does सुंदर (sundar) not agree? (It does not end in -आ; it arrived from Sanskrit already finished.) What does the सु- in it mean? (Good, well — as in सुद्धा.)
Sources: Wiktionary: सुंदर (sundar).

lessons.title: The last letter decides
lessons.gloss: three adjectives, two classes, and one test that tells them apart

segments.text: Three adjectives are now yours. Sort them into two classes before you say anything with them.

segments.instruction: moṭhī khoolī, lahān khoolī, sundar khoolī
which of the three moved, and why — मोठा, because it ends in -आ
segments.source: [YOU SAY: which of the three moved, and why — ***मोठा***, because it ends in **-आ**]

segments.instruction: say mitrāśī and tell your friend the room is beautiful
segments.source: [YOU RECALL: say *mitrāśī* and tell your friend the room is beautiful]

segments.prompt: Put all three adjectives on khoolī, and say which one changed.
acceptedResponses: moṭhī khoolī; lahān khoolī; sundar khoolī — only moṭhā changed
मोठी खोली लहान खोली सुंदर खोली

feedback.incorrect: Only the -ā adjective takes an ending.

segments.text: What is the one test that sorts every Marathi adjective into its class? (Does it end in -आ?) Where do all three of them stand? (Before the noun.)
